newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola sharply down on commercial, local sales.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola sharply down on commercial, local sales.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended sharply down on commercial and local selling, traders said.

"Commercials sold on the close, there was local and hedge selling. We're down on the weak soyoil," a trader said. Four hundred May-Nov spread at $53.50, Mar-May $2.50, May-July $1. May WCE futures crush profit margin fell to -18.93 Monday from -14.35 Friday. Volume was 7,588 lots with 1,750 hedges.
Japan bought 3,000-5,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
May canola lost $8.30 to $423.20, July down $8.20 to $423.50 and November fell $9 to $368.20. May flax lost $4 to $355 as 100 hedges were met by exporter demand. Volume 300.
May feed wheat fell $0.90 to $173.10 as commercial demand at the close and CBOT corn raised values, December down $0.50 to $165. Mar-May spread at $10. Volume was 875 lots.
May western barley fell $2.50 to $142.70 under hedge pressure, July lost $2 to $140.60 on commercial and local selling. Volume was 950 lots. Oats did not trade.
Commercials sold 25 December feed pea contracts down the US$5 limit at US$187.50 to Cargill, 35 December to RBC-DS and 25 October down US$4 at US$188.50 to RBC-DS, traders said.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas)
